questions.question: The simple interest on a sum is 5/9 of the principal for 25 years. What is the rate (in percentage) of interest per annum?
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a sum is 5/9 of the principal for 25 years. What is the rate (in percentage) of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the Principal be 9 units, then Simple Interest (SI) = 5 units.

Time (T) = 25 years.

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

R = (5 × 100) ÷ (9 × 25) = 500 ÷ 225

R = 20/9 %

∴ The correct answer is 20/9 %.

Alternate Method

Given:

Simple Interest (SI) = 5/9 of Principal (P)

Time (T) = 25 years

Formula Used:

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ (5/9)P = (P × R × 25) ÷ 100

⇒ 5/9 = (25 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 5/9 = R ÷ 4

⇒ R = (5 × 4) ÷ 9

⇒ R = 20/9 %

∴ The correct answer is 20/9 %.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the initial principal sum for the entire duration of the loan. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount (A)

The total accumulated sum at the end of the time period consisting of the principal and simple interest combined. Formula: A = P + SI = P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Rate of Interest

The percentage of the principal charged or earned per unit time. Computed directly by R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).

questions.question: The tops of two poles of height 15 m and 27 m are connected by a cable. If the cable makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal, then find the length of the cable.
questions.questionHtml: The tops of two poles of height 15 m and 27 m are connected by a cable. If the cable makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal, then find the length of the cable.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in heights of the poles = Perpendicular side = 27 − 15 = 12 m.

The connecting cable acts as the hypotenuse making a 60° angle with the horizontal base.

Using trigonometry: sin(60°) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

⇒ √3 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ Cable Length

⇒ Cable Length = 24 ÷ √3 = 8√3 m

∴ The correct answer is 8√3 meter.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of the smaller pole (AB) = 15 m

Height of the taller pole (CD) = 27 m

Angle of elevation of the cable from the horizontal = 60°


Formula Used:

sin(θ) = Opposite side ÷ Hypotenuse

sin(60°) = √3 ÷ 2


Calculations:

⇒ From the diagram, draw a horizontal line AE from the top of the first pole to the second pole.

⇒ Length of CE = CD − ED

⇒ CE = 27 − 15 = 12 m

⇒ In right-angled triangle AEC, the connecting cable is AC (Hypotenuse).

⇒ sin(60°) = CE ÷ AC

⇒ √3 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ AC

⇒ AC = (12 × 2) ÷ √3

⇒ AC = 24 ÷ √3

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying and dividing by √3:

⇒ AC = (24√3) ÷ 3

⇒ AC = 8√3 m

∴ The correct answer is 8√3 meter.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios (Right-Angled Triangle)

sin(θ) = Opposite/Hypotenuse | cos(θ) = Adjacent/Hypotenuse | tan(θ) = Opposite/Adjacent.

Standard Trigonometric Values

sin(30°) = 1/2, sin(45°) = 1/√2, sin(60°) = √3/2.

Angle of Elevation & Depression

Elevation is the angle above the horizontal line of sight; depression is the angle below. Both are equal when forming alternate interior angles.

questions.question: Find the average speed of a boy if he walks 1/3rd distance with a speed of 2 m/sec and rides a bike to cover the remaining distance with a speed of 12 m/s. The total distance is 1.44 km.
questions.questionHtml: Find the average speed of a boy if he walks 1/3rd distance with a speed of 2 m/sec and rides a bike to cover the remaining distance with a speed of 12 m/s. The total distance is 1.44 km.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When distances are given as fractions, the average speed is independent of the total distance.

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 1 ÷ [(1/3 ÷ 2) + (2/3 ÷ 12)]

⇒ Average Speed = 1 ÷ (1/6 + 2/36) = 1 ÷ (4/18) = 9/2 = 4.5 m/s

⇒ Average Speed in km/hr = 4.5 × (18/5) = 16.2 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 16.2 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance = 1.44 km = 1440 m

Speed while walking (S1) = 2 m/s

Speed while riding a bike (S2) = 12 m/s

Formula Used:

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:

⇒ 1/3rd of the total distance = 1/3 × 1440 = 480 m

⇒ Time taken to walk (T1) = 480 ÷ 2 = 240 seconds

⇒ Remaining 2/3rd distance = 1440 − 480 = 960 m

⇒ Time taken by bike (T2) = 960 ÷ 12 = 80 seconds

⇒ Total Time = 240 + 80 = 320 seconds

⇒ Average Speed = 1440 ÷ 320 = 4.5 m/s

⇒ Average Speed in km/hr = 4.5 × (18/5) = 16.2 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 16.2 km/hr.

Additional Information

Average Speed

It is defined as the ratio of total distance travelled to the total time taken for the entire journey. Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Special Case for Equal Distances

If an object covers two equal halves of a journey at speeds S1 and S2 respectively, the average speed simplifies to (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from m/s to km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5. To convert from km/hr back to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

questions.question: A tank can be filled by a pipe P in 32 minutes and by pipe Q in 36 minutes. When it is full, it can be emptied by a pipe R in 20 minutes. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, half of the tank will be filled in ________.
questions.questionHtml: A tank can be filled by a pipe P in 32 minutes and by pipe Q in 36 minutes. When it is full, it can be emptied by a pipe R in 20 minutes. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, half of the tank will be filled in ________.
questions.solution:
⇒ Efficiency of pipe P = 1/32

⇒ Efficiency of pipe Q = 1/36

⇒ Tank emptied by Pipe R in 1 minute = 1/20

 Half Tank filled in 1 minutes when all the three pipes are opened = 1 / 2{1/32 + 1/36 - 1/20} = 720/13 = \(55\frac{5}{13}\;minutes\)

questions.question: After allowing a discount of \(12\frac{1}{2}\) % on the marked price of an article. it was sold for ₹700. Had the discount NOT been given, the profit would have been 60%.The cost price of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: After allowing a discount of \(12\frac{1}{2}\)% on the marked price of an article. it was sold for ₹700. Had the discount NOT been given, the profit would have been 60%.The cost price of the article is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Discount = 12.5% = 1/8 ⇒ SP = (1 − 1/8) × MP = 7/8 of MP.

Given SP = ₹700 ⇒ 7/8 × MP = 700 ⇒ MP = ₹800.

If no discount is given, SP = MP = ₹800.

Profit = 60% = 3/5 ⇒ SP = (1 + 3/5) × CP = 8/5 of CP.

Since SP = ₹800 ⇒ 8/5 × CP = 800 ⇒ CP = ₹500.

∴ The correct answer is ₹500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price (SP) = ₹700

Discount = 12.5%

Profit without discount = 60%

Formula Used:

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Marked Price be MP.

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − 12.5) ÷ 100

⇒ 700 = MP × 87.5 ÷ 100

⇒ 700 = MP × 7 ÷ 8

⇒ MP = 700 × 8 ÷ 7 = ₹800

⇒ If no discount is given, the selling price equals the marked price.

⇒ New SP = ₹800

⇒ Profit% in this case = 60%

⇒ New SP = CP × (100 + 60) ÷ 100

⇒ 800 = CP × 160 ÷ 100

⇒ 800 = CP × 8 ÷ 5

⇒ CP = 800 × 5 ÷ 8 = ₹500

∴ The correct answer is ₹500.

Additional Information

Marked Price and Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the printed price of an article. Discount is always calculated on the MP. Formula: SP = MP − Discount.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

A highly useful formula linking Cost Price and Marked Price directly is: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d1% and d2% are given, the equivalent single discount is (d1 + d2 − d1×d2 / 100)%.

questions.question: The supplement of an angle is 15° more than three times its complement. The measure of the angle is:
questions.questionHtml: The supplement of an angle is 15° more than three times its complement. The measure of the angle is:
questions.solution:
Concept Used:

In this type of question, supplement of angle = 180° – x,

Complement of angle = 90° – x

Calculation:

Let angle be x°

According to the question,

180° – x = 3(90° – x) + 15°

⇒ 180° – x° = 270° – 3x° + 15°

⇒ 2x = 105

⇒ x = 52.5

∴ The measure of the angle is 52.5°.

questions.question: If there are 20 boys and 40 girls in a class and the average age of the boys is 13 years and that of the girls is 14 years, determine the approximate average age of the class.
questions.questionHtml: If there are 20 boys and 40 girls in a class and the average age of the boys is 13 years and that of the girls is 14 years, determine the approximate average age of the class.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Boys to Girls = 20 : 40 = 1 : 2.

Let assumed average of the class be 13 years (Boys' average).

Deviation for girls = 14 − 13 = +1 year.

Total net deviation for 2 units of girls = +1 × 2 = +2 years.

Average deviation across all 3 units = +2 ÷ 3 ≈ +0.67 years.

Combined class average = 13 + 0.67 = 13.67 years.

∴ The correct answer is 13.67 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of boys (n1) = 20

Average age of boys (A1) = 13 years

Number of girls (n2) = 40

Average age of girls (A2) = 14 years

Formula Used:

Combined Average = (n1 × A1 + n2 × A2) ÷ (n1 + n2)

Calculations:

⇒ Total age of boys = 20 × 13 = 260 years

⇒ Total age of girls = 40 × 14 = 560 years

⇒ Total age of the class = 260 + 560 = 820 years

⇒ Total number of students = 20 + 40 = 60

⇒ Combined Average = 820 ÷ 60

⇒ Combined Average = 82 ÷ 6 = 41 ÷ 3

⇒ Combined Average ≈ 13.67 years

∴ The correct answer is 13.67 years.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups have different sizes and different averages, the combined average is calculated as (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Alligation Method

Used to find the ratio of quantities when two different groups are mixed. The final ratio of the two groups corresponds to (Dearer Avg − Combined Avg) : (Combined Avg − Cheaper Avg).

Deviation Method for Averages

Instead of performing lengthy total calculations, you can assume a base average and distribute the net deviation among the total items to find the exact average easily.

questions.question: A cube of side 15 cm is cut into 27 small cubes. Then find the ratio of the lateral surface area of the large cube to the total surface area of one of the small cubes.
questions.questionHtml: A cube of side 15 cm is cut into 27 small cubes. Then find the ratio of the lateral surface area of the large cube to the total surface area of one of the small cubes.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number of small cubes = (A/a)3 = 27 ⇒ Ratio of sides (A/a) = 3.

Ratio of areas = (Lateral Surface Area of Large Cube) ÷ (Total Surface Area of Small Cube)

⇒ (4 × A2) ÷ (6 × a2)

⇒ (4/6) × (A/a)2 = (2/3) × 32 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6 : 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the large cube (A) = 15 cm

Number of small cubes formed = 27

Formula Used:

Volume of cube = (side)3

Lateral Surface Area of cube = 4 × (side)2

Total Surface Area of cube = 6 × (side)2

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of large cube = 27 × Volume of small cube

⇒ 153 = 27 × a3

⇒ 3375 = 27 × a3

⇒ a3 = 125 ⇒ a = 5 cm

⇒ Lateral Surface Area of large cube = 4 × 152 = 4 × 225 = 900 cm2

⇒ Total Surface Area of small cube = 6 × 52 = 6 × 25 = 150 cm2

⇒ Required Ratio = 900 / 150 = 6 / 1 = 6 : 1

∴ The correct answer is 6 : 1.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of a Cube

It is the sum of the areas of all 6 faces of the cube. Formula: TSA = 6 × (side)2

Lateral Surface Area of a Cube

It is the sum of the areas of the 4 vertical side faces of the cube, excluding the top and bottom faces. Formula: LSA = 4 × (side)2

Volume of a Cube

It represents the total 3D space occupied by the cube. When a shape is cut or reshaped, the total volume remains conserved. Formula: Volume = (side)3

questions.question: If a circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side a cm, then find the ratio of their area.
questions.questionHtml: If a circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side a cm, then find the ratio of their area.
questions.solution:
Formula:

Area of triangle = [√3/4] × a2                       (a = side)

Area of circle = πr2                                           (r = radius)

Radius of in-circle = a/2√3

Calculation:

Radius of in-circle = a/2√3

⇒ Area of circle = π × [a/2√3]2 = π × [a2/12]

Area of triangle = [√3/4] × a2

∴ Required ratio = π × [a2/12] : [√3/4] × a2 = π : 3√3

questions.question: Average of ‘n’ observations is 38, average of ‘n’ other observations is 42 and average of remaining ‘n’ observations is 55. Average of all the observations is:
questions.questionHtml: Average of ‘n’ observations is 38, average of ‘n’ other observations is 42 and average of remaining ‘n’ observations is 55. Average of all the observations is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the number of observations in all three groups is equal ('n'), the overall average is simply the arithmetic mean of their individual averages.

Overall Average = (Sum of all averages) ÷ (Number of groups)

Overall Average = (38 + 42 + 55) ÷ 3

Overall Average = 135 ÷ 3 = 45

∴ The correct answer is 45.

Alternate Method

Given:

Three groups of observations, each containing 'n' observations.

Averages of the three groups are 38, 42, and 55 respectively.

Formula Used:

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

Overall Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Total Number of Observations

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of first 'n' observations = 38 × n = 38n

⇒ Sum of second 'n' observations = 42 × n = 42n

⇒ Sum of remaining 'n' observations = 55 × n = 55n

⇒ Total sum of all observations = 38n + 42n + 55n = 135n

⇒ Total number of observations = n + n + n = 3n

⇒ Overall average = 135n ÷ 3n

⇒ Overall average = 45

∴ The correct answer is 45.

Additional Information

Combined Average

When combining multiple groups with different numbers of items (n1, n2, ...), the combined average is given by the weighted average formula: A = (n1A1 + n2A2 + ...) ÷ (n1 + n2 + ...).

Equal Weights Shortcut

If the number of items in all combined groups is identical (n1 = n2 = n3 ...), the combined average simplifies to the basic arithmetic mean of the individual averages: (A1 + A2 + A3 + ...) ÷ Total Groups.

Net Deviation Method

Assume an arbitrary mean (e.g., 40). Find the net deviation of each group's average from it. The final average is calculated as: Assumed Mean + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Number of Items). This technique helps in fast mental calculations.

questions.question: With a 10% discount on the marked price, a seller earns a 5% profit. If the marked price is increased by 5% and two successive discounts of 5% each are offered, how much percentage profit does the seller earn?
questions.questionHtml: With a 10% discount on the marked price, a seller earns a 5% profit. If the marked price is increased by 5% and two successive discounts of 5% each are offered, how much percentage profit does the seller earn?
questions.solution:
Let's assume the marked price is Rs. 100.

With a 10% discount on the marked price, the selling price would be:

Selling price = 100 - (10/100) × 100 ⇒ 100 - 10 = 90

Cost Price when there is 5% profit = 90 × 100/(100 + 5)

Cost price = 90 × 100/105, Cost price =  Rs. 85.71

Now, let's consider the scenario where the marked price is increased by 5% and two successive discounts of 5% each are offered.

The new marked price = 100 + (5/100) × 100 ⇒ 100 + 5 = 105

Selling price = Marked price ×  (100 - Discount%)/100

Selling price = 105 ×  (100 - 5)/100 ×  (100 - 5)/100 = 94.76

Profit percentage ⇒ ((94.76 - 85.71)/85.71) × 100 ⇒ (9.05/85.71) × 100 ⇒ 10.5

Time Efficiency Total work

questions.question: A Person bought a pre-owned camera for Rs. 85000 and spent additional Rs. 4500 for memory cards and Rs 5500 for the tripod. Then he sold the whole kit for Rs. 100000. Find the profit or loss %.
questions.questionHtml: A Person bought a pre-owned camera for Rs. 85000 and spent additional Rs. 4500 for memory cards and Rs 5500 for the tripod. Then he sold the whole kit for Rs. 100000. Find the profit or loss %.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total CP = 85000 + 4500 + 5500 = 95000

Selling Price (SP) = 100000

Profit = 100000 − 95000 = 5000

Profit % = (5000 ÷ 95000) × 100 = 100 ÷ 19 ≈ 5.26%

∴ The correct answer is 5.26% profit.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost price of camera = Rs. 85000

Amount spent on memory cards = Rs. 4500

Amount spent on tripod = Rs. 5500

Selling price of the whole kit = Rs. 100000

Formula Used:

Total CP = Initial CP + Overhead Expenses

Profit = SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Total CP = 85000 + 4500 + 5500 = Rs. 95000

⇒ Profit = 100000 − 95000 = Rs. 5000

⇒ Profit % = (5000 ÷ 95000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 19) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 100 ÷ 19

⇒ Profit % = 5.263... ≈ 5.26%

∴ The correct answer is 5.26% profit.

Additional Information

Overhead Expenses

Any additional amount spent on transportation, repairs, or accessories must always be added to the initial Cost Price to find the Total Cost Price before calculating profit or loss.

Loss Percentage

When Selling Price is less than the Total Cost Price, Loss is incurred. The formula is Loss % = (Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), not the Cost Price. The Selling Price is equal to MP − Discount.

questions.question: The downstream speed of a boat is 25 km / hr and the speed of stream is 3 km / hr . What will be the total time taken by the boat to cover 100 km downstream and 57 km upstream?
questions.questionHtml: The downstream speed of a boat is 25 km/hr and the speed of stream is 3 km/hr. What will be the total time taken by the boat to cover 100 km downstream and 57 km upstream?
questions.solution:
The speed of the boat in still water = 25 km/hr - 3 km/hr = 22 km/hr.

When the boat is moving downstream = 22 km/hr + 3 km/hr = 25 km/hr.

When the boat is moving upstream  = 22 km/hr - 3 km/hr = 19 km/hr.

To travel 100 km downstream, the boat will take 100 km / 25 km/hr = 4 hours.

To travel 57 km upstream, the boat will take 57 km / 19 km/hr = 3 hours.

Required Time=  4 hours + 3 hours = 7 hours.

questions.question: The numbers of boys and girls in a college are in the ratio of 5 ∶ 3. If 24% of the boys and 32% of the girls were not placed in campus placements, then the percentage of students who got jobs in campus placements is:
questions.questionHtml: The numbers of boys and girls in a college are in the ratio of 5 ∶ 3. If 24% of the boys and 32% of the girls were not placed in campus placements, then the percentage of students who got jobs in campus placements is:
questions.solution:
Let the total number of students be 800.

Boys placements = 100% - 24% = 76% ⇒ 76% of 500 = 380

Girls placements = 100% - 32% = 68% ⇒ 68% of 300 = 204

Total placements = 380 + 204 = 584

∴ Percentage of placements = (584/800) × 100 = 73%

questions.question: If (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C, then what is the value of A ∶ B ∶ C?
questions.questionHtml: If (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C, then what is the value of A ∶ B ∶ C?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Equate the given expression to 1: (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C = 1

⇒ A = 3, B = 1/3, C = 4/3

⇒ A : B : C = 3 : 1/3 : 4/3

Multiply by 3 to eliminate the denominators:

⇒ A : B : C = 9 : 1 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 9 : 1 : 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C

Formula Used:

If xA = yB = zC = k, then A : B : C = (k/x) : (k/y) : (k/z)

Calculations:

Let (1/3)A = 3B = (3/4)C = k

⇒ A = 3k

⇒ B = k/3

⇒ C = 4k/3

Now, substitute the values of A, B, and C into the ratio form A : B : C:

⇒ A : B : C = 3k : k/3 : 4k/3

Divide the entire ratio by k:

⇒ A : B : C = 3 : 1/3 : 4/3

Multiply all terms by the least common multiple of the denominators (LCM of 3 is 3):

⇒ A : B : C = (3 × 3) : (1/3 × 3) : (4/3 × 3)

⇒ A : B : C = 9 : 1 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 9 : 1 : 4.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two or more ratios is obtained by multiplying their antecedent and consequent terms respectively. For a : b and c : d, it is (a × c) : (b × d).

Inverse Ratio

The inverse ratio of a : b is b : a. If aA = bB, then the ratio A : B is equal to b : a.

Duplicate & Triplicate Ratios

The duplicate ratio of a : b is given as a2 : b2, and the triplicate ratio is a3 : b3.

questions.question: The ratio of the efficiencies of A, B and C is 4 ∶ 5 ∶ 3. Working together, they can complete that work in 25 days. A and C together will complete 35% of that work in:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the efficiencies of A, B and C is 4 ∶ 5 ∶ 3. Working together, they can complete that work in 25 days. A and C together will complete 35% of that work in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio A : B : C = 4 : 5 : 3

Total efficiency = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 units/day

Total work = 12 × 25 = 300 units

35% of work = 300 × 0.35 = 105 units

Efficiency of (A + C) = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day

Time taken = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 days

∴ The correct option is B.

Alternate Method

Given: Efficiency ratio of A, B and C is 4 : 5 : 3. They complete work in 25 days.

Formula Used: Total Work = (Combined Efficiency) × Time

Combined efficiency of A + B + C = 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 units/day

Total work = 12 × 25 = 300 units

⇒ Target work = 35% of 300

⇒ Target work = (35 ÷ 100) × 300 = 105 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and C = 4 + 3 = 7 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and C = 105 ÷ 7 = 15 days

∴ The correct option is B.

Additional Information

Relationship between Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a specific task (Efficiency ∝ 1 ÷ Time). If efficiency doubles, time taken is halved.

Total Work Calculation

Total work can be calculated by multiplying the combined efficiency of the group by the total number of days taken: Work = (Σ Efficiencies) × Total Days.

Work & Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the work done by each individual, which is the product of their efficiency and the time for which they worked.

questions.question: A sum of ₹2,50,000 is invested for one and a half years at 12% per annum compound interest. What is the difference between the amounts received when the interest is compounded semi-annually and when it is compounded annually?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of ₹2,50,000 is invested for one and a half years at 12% per annum compound interest. What is the difference between the amounts received when the interest is compounded semi-annually and when it is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective CI rate (annually) for 1.5 years at 12% = 12% + 6% + (12 × 6) ÷ 100 = 18.72%

Effective CI rate (semi-annually) for 3 half-years at 6% = 3(6) + 3(6)2 ÷ 100 + (6)3 ÷ 10000 = 18 + 1.08 + 0.0216 = 19.1016%

Difference in effective rate = 19.1016% − 18.72% = 0.3816%

Difference in amount = 0.3816% of 2,50,000 = (0.3816 ÷ 100) × 250000 = ₹954

∴ The correct answer is ₹954.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹2,50,000

Rate (R) = 12% per annum

Time (T) = 1.5 years

Calculations:

⇒ Amount compounded annually (A1) = P × (1 + R/100)1 × (1 + (R/2)/100)

⇒ A1 = 250000 × (1 + 12/100) × (1 + 6/100)

⇒ A1 = 250000 × 1.12 × 1.06 = 250000 × 1.1872

⇒ A1 = ₹2,96,800


⇒ Amount compounded semi-annually (A2) = P × (1 + (R/2)/100)2T

⇒ A2 = 250000 × (1 + 6/100)3

⇒ A2 = 250000 × (1.06)3 = 250000 × 1.191016

⇒ A2 = ₹2,97,754


⇒ Difference in amounts = A2 − A1

⇒ Difference = 297754 − 296800 = ₹954

∴ The correct answer is ₹954.

Additional Information

Effective Rate Method

For 3 equal periods at rate R%, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as: 3R + 3R2/100 + R3/10000.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded semi-annually, the annual rate of interest is divided by 2 (R/2) and the number of years is multiplied by 2 (2T).

Fractional Year Compounding

If time is given in fractions like 1.5 years, the formula used for annual compounding is: A = P(1 + R/100)1 × (1 + (R/2)/100)1.
